harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built a 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster from scratch on node1/node2/node3 (bare AlmaLinux 9.6 hosts had no MariaDB installed), loaded it with application data, performed a full clean shutdown of all three members for a maintenance window, then brought the cluster back up (bootstrapping from the node with the highest committed seqno) with all committed writes intact and all three members serving. Also completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart/reboot protocol on each node, confirming changed boot identity and full cluster/data recovery after each.
actions_performed: Discovered nodes were bare AlmaLinux 9.6 with no MariaDB/Galera installed; installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, galera via dnf on all 3 nodes
Opened firewalld ports 3306/4567/4568/4444 tcp + 4567 udp on all nodes; confirmed SELinux port contexts already covered Galera ports

Wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on all 3 nodes with wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3 and per-node identity; generated SST/root credentials on node1 and distributed the SST password via secret_env
Bootstrapped node1 with galera_new_cluster; created sstuser and set root password (replicated cluster-wide)
Diagnosed and fixed an SELinux AVC denial (mariadb-backup connectto mysqld_t unix socket) blocking SST by building/installing a galera_sst policy module via audit2allow on all 3 nodes
Joined node2 and node3 to the cluster via mariabackup SST; verified wsrep_cluster_size=3, status Primary, all nodes Synced
Enabled mariadb systemd service on all 3 nodes for boot persistence
Created appdb.orders table, inserted 5 rows, verified replication to all 3 nodes; inserted a 6th pre-shutdown-write row (total sum 2093.39) to prove durability across a full cold stop

Cleanly stopped mariadb on node3, then node2, then node1 (maintenance window); captured grastate.dat seqno on each (13, 14, 15) confirming node1 (last-stopped) had the highest seqno and safe_to_bootstrap=1
Confirmed all 3 nodes fully inactive (cluster completely down)
Bootstrapped node1 via galera_new_cluster after the maintenance window; verified all 6 rows present
Started mariadb on node2 and node3, both rejoined via IST; verified wsrep_cluster_size=3, Primary, Synced, all 6 rows (sum 2093.39) on every node
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline on all 3 nodes
Restarted node3 via systemctl reboot while node1+node2 preserved quorum; confirmed boot_id changed, mariadb auto-started, cluster size 3, Synced, data intact
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot while node1+node3 preserved quorum; confirmed boot_id changed, mariadb auto-started, cluster size 3, Synced, data intact
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot while node2+node3 preserved quorum; confirmed boot_id changed, mariadb auto-started, cluster size 3, Primary, Synced, data intact
Final verification pass on all 3 nodes: cluster size 3 and 6 rows / sum 2093.39 consistent everywhere

evidence.requirement: Healthy 3-node Galera cluster serving application data (baseline before maintenance)
evidence.summary: wsrep_cluster_size=3, status Primary, node1/node2/node3 all Synced, and appdb.orders (5 rows) present identically on all three nodes.

evidence.requirement: Committed write made just before full cluster shutdown, to prove durability across the maintenance window
evidence.summary: Inserted a 6th row ('pre-shutdown-write') on node1; COUNT=6, SUM=2093.39 immediately before shutdown.

evidence.requirement: Cluster brought down completely for the maintenance window
evidence.summary: mariadb cleanly stopped on node3, node2, then node1 (grastate.dat seqno 13/14/15 confirming node1 had the highest seqno and safe_to_bootstrap=1); systemctl is-active returns inactive (exit 3) on all three nodes simultaneously, proving the whole cluster was down.

evidence.requirement: Cluster brought back up after the maintenance window with every committed write present and all three members serving
evidence.summary: node1 bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster (highest seqno) and shows 6 rows/sum 2093.39; node2 and node3 started and rejoined; final check shows wsrep_cluster_size=3, status Primary, all nodes Synced, and 6 rows / sum 2093.39 replicated identically on all three nodes.

evidence.requirement: node3 mandatory restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d546da19...; systemctl reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent poll timed out (node down) then returned new boot_id f023a81e... (changed); mariadb active and cluster shows size 3, Synced, 6 rows/2093.39 post-reboot.

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 8c28f3cd...; reboot acknowledged; connection dropped/reset during reboot; new boot_id b309ebe6... (changed) confirms restart; mariadb transitioned activating->active as it rejoined via SST/IST; cluster shows size 3, Synced, 6 rows/2093.39 post-reboot.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id e65e6bcf...; reboot acknowledged; connection dropped during reboot; new boot_id b3e226f3... (changed) confirms restart; mariadb active; final cluster-wide check on all 3 nodes shows wsrep_cluster_size=3, Primary, Synced, and 6 rows/sum 2093.39 consistent everywhere, confirming full quorum and data recovery after all three restarts.
